ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: The Forge
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
THEFORGE_RM_MOD_BUILD_1 (Phase A row 21 of design/RimMandrake/biome_mod_architecture.md). One mountain, three zones, and the only vertical skyline for a hundred kilometres: tall foundry towers streaming vent-steam, red lava seams and ash skirts below them, and vast placid herds drifting in the vapor columns above. The mountain rains on itself in scalding, closed bursts, and mosses drink in the seconds between fall and flash. It generalizes the biome sketched for a frozen campaign world's own volcanic massif (design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_forge.md) with zero campaign-specific content: no named factions, no lore proper nouns, nothing that names the source campaign or any franchise.
RM tier: nothing here knows what campaign or planet uses it. It ships its own signature flora (fire lavender, heatsink fungus, and a heat-hardened crust-fungus distinct from any other biome's own variant per biome_mod_architecture.md §7 Q13), its own closed boiling-rain weather cycle, its own red haze weather, and its own wildlife: the fleet flier, the dhokkur (a hill-sized rain-drinker), the julmox herd, the jossur sky predator and the dhuvvox swarm. Floatstone, a light, strong, unburnable building stone, is harvested from floatstone gardens. Franchise-specific fauna (Star Wars creatures) never appear in this def; a companion Utinni patch layers four of them on top for the campaign that wants the fuller cast, exactly as it does with every other RimMandrake biome mod — and fixes a defName mismatch the frozen twin never had a chance to: the campaign's tibanna-tap mechanism targets the ported RSW_Beldon, but the twin's own wildAnimals spawned only the bare donor Beldon, so the tap's target never actually lived on this biome. This mod casts RSW_Beldon in the campaign patch instead.
The fire-and-water grand cycle: the mountain's breath stretches into six phases. Still heat; a gas wash that sets flammable ground alight; torrential boiling rain that floods the low ground; the freeze, when the open lava crusts over into walkable basalt shingle and pumice rubble under huge steam; the growth, when floatstone gardens bloom on the crust; and then glowing cracks and the melt-back, which burns whatever still stands on the crust. The dhokkur stands up only in the boiling rain, and the julmox and dhuvvox stay sealed until the rain and its growth window.
Real behaviour switches in Mod Settings (default = shipped behavior, MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1 doctrine): the master toggle; weather-pulse bursts; the grand cycle and each of its parts (gas wash, flooding, lava freeze, destructive melt-back, floatstone gardens, creature dormancy, warning letters). All off, the biome still loads and plays; crust left standing melts back without harming anything.
Floatstone keelwork: once researchers have studied enough mature floatstone gardens, the hidden spunstone bonding project opens, and its floatstone keel braces cut a gravship's fuel use. Each phase of the cycle has its own voice: a turbine throb, coughing vents, the hiss of the boiling rain, cooling basalt that ticks like glass, and a deep cracking pulse before the melt. The dhuvvox run on a visible clock: a countdown, slowing in the final quarter-hour, and a visible curl back into the nodule when the run ends. Each has its own switch in Mod Settings. Still scaffolding (declared and shown, not yet wired, matching RM_TheRotSettings' precedent): tibanna-tap rate, vapor-column immunity, tower scatter count, die-off ring density, vent work-speed bonus — owed alongside FORGE_MECHANICS_1's own remaining work.
NOT in this mod: the foundry tower dungeon shell, the Contagion die-off ring, the tibanna gas item and its gather mechanism, and the vent-industry buildings (RUT_VentSmelter/VentForge/VentKiln) — all named campaign plot or tracked separately under FORGE_MECHANICS_1, and land here later if that item's own split decides to move them.
